- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak by 5–10% and smooth transition.
- If model consistently underestimates after a recent price dip, consider mean reversion bias — add 2–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model likely missed upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction — favor longer-term sentiment average over short-term spikes.
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ days, consider lag error — model is reacting too late; adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits noise — use 3-day moving average or median of recent 5-day forecast for smoothing.
